item.title: Trump Calls Putin 'My Friend' as Xi Prepares to Host Trilateral Meeting
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
President Donald Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin held their first in-person meeting in more than a year on the sidelines of a gathering in China Thursday. Meanwhile Xi Jinping and Donald Trump spoke fondly of each other at their third meeting this year.
Plus, Anthropic shares are indicated to open between 20% and 26% higher in gray market trading after the artificial intelligence lab’s upsized $107.3 billion initial public offering and private placement broke SpaceX’s record.
Today's guest: David Sher, AMC Group, Managing Director. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Public Investment Fund’s Riyadh Headquarters Damaged
item.description: The skyscraper housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in Riyadh was damaged, according to an eyewitness.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: South Korea Blasts Mobile Emergency Alerts To Catch Exam Cheats
item.description: Thursday morning phones across South Korea blared a loud beeping alarm for about 10 seconds, as the government deployed an “extreme emergency alert” typically used to warn of natural disasters. This time it was meant to prevent AI-assisted cheating on the annual college-entrance exam.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Kim

item.title: Trump Calls Xi a 'Friend' as Leaders Hold Talks in China
item.description: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump spoke fondly of each other at their third meeting this year, showing little sign that a fresh fight over chip curbs immediately threatens a broader truce between the world’s two largest economies. Bloomberg’s Minmin Low reports from Shenzhen. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia Lawmakers Pass Long-Debated Asset Forfeiture Law
item.description: Indonesia’s parliament on Thursday approved a long-debated asset forfeiture law, giving authorities greater power in some cases to seize suspected criminal proceeds without first securing a conviction.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Finland Shuns Unproven Kit as Army Overhaul Grows Shopping List
item.description: Finland’s Army has an exacting list of demands for would-be suppliers as works through an overhaul of more than €11 billion ($12 billion).
item.dc:creator: Kirsi Heikel

item.title: Erdogan Widens Fund-Scandal Crackdown to Limit Political Fallout
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is pressing officials to move against more of those implicated in the country’s fund scandal and accelerate repayments to hundreds of thousands of investors, a bid to limit the political fallout for his government.
item.dc:creator: Selcan Hacaoglu and Firat Kozok

item.title: China Says Xi-Trump Talks Positive, Hails Stable Relations
item.description: Xi Jinping called his meeting with Donald Trump “positive and constructive,” signaling efforts remain on track to preserve a trade truce between the world’s two largest economies despite renewed tensions over US chip curbs.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: UK Healthcare Managers Warn Youth Reforms Could Hinder Staffing
item.description: Staff in the UK’s National Health Service are concerned that UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s efforts to get more young people into work could have the unwanted effect of creating a shortage of senior health workers.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Geopolitical Analyst on Competing Views in Trilateral
item.description: Senior Vice President of Studies at the Council on Foreign Relations Shannon O’Neil downplays comparisons to Yalta - when in 1945, the leaders of the three dominant military powers gathered to craft a plan that would bring stability to the world or, depending on your reading, conspired to carve it up among themselves - and says the agenda of trilateral talks between US President Donald Trump and his counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin is unclear. O’Neill points to denuclearization and AI as issues that may be discussed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Meets Putin for First Time in 15 Months, Talks Ukraine
item.description: President Donald Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin discussed Ukraine during their first in-person meeting in more than a year Thursday on the sidelines of a gathering of world leaders in China.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason, Courtney Subramanian and Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: What’s Next After Trump, Xi, Putin Meet for Historic Trilateral?: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions on Nov 19 at 5 p.m. HKT / 9 a.m. GMT
item.dc:creator: Dan Strumpf, Jeff Mason, Nectar Gan and Paul Abelsky

item.title: GOP’s Begich Holds Alaska House Seat, Resisting Democratic Tide
item.description: Republican Nick Begich fended off a surprisingly strong challenge from independent candidate Bill Hill, keeping Alaska’s at-large House seat in Republican hands even as the state’s Senate and governor’s races flipped toward Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Anna Edgerton

item.title: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser at Bloomberg Newsmakers Event
item.description: Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser discusses the expected Anthropic initial public offering, the recent tech outages across the US and working with President Donald Trump and newly elected Democratic leaders in Congress. She speaks with Lisa Abramowicz at a Bloomberg Newsmakers event in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Pushes for Reluctant Xi to Curb China’s Nuclear Arsenal
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would like China to stop building up its nuclear arsenal, a request that Xi Jinping is almost certain to rebuff if it’s brought up during an unprecedented trilateral meeting including the two leaders and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Trump Hails Great Ties With Xi, Downplays Nvidia Controversy
item.description: US President Donald Trump hailed his great “friendship” with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and downplayed a spying controversy involving Nvidia Corp., hours before leaders of the world’s top economies meet for talks.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Trump Suggests US Can Sell Blackwell Chips to China in Future
item.description: President Donald Trump said that the US could potentially allow the sale of Nvidia Corp.’s highly sought Blackwell chips to China in the future, when they were no longer among the most advanced on the market.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Maggie Eastland

item.title: Maria Corina Machado Questions Trump Oil Deal While Committing to US Ties
item.description: The US government’s $100 billion deal with a controversial Venezuelan oil baron needs scrutiny, but a long-term partnership with Washington is nevertheless critical for Caracas, said opposition leader María Corina Machado.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Garip and Andreina Itriago

item.title: UK Pledges Long-Range Missiles to Ukraine Amid US Criticism
item.description: The UK pledged to send 1,000 long-range cruise missiles to Ukraine, in a pointed signal of British support for strikes deep inside Russia that have been criticized by the US.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Putin in Spotlight of APEC Photos After Decade of Isolation
item.description: Vladimir Putin appeared in a “family photo” of APEC leaders for the first time in nine years, taking a central position alongside Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in a powerful rebuff of Western efforts to isolate him on the world stage.
item.dc:creator: Jenni Marsh
